campaigns.title: Help abandoned elderly with shelter and care
campaigns.description: 1 in 4 elders in urban India is abused by their own son or daughter-in-law.Every day, elderly parents are left alone on streets, at railway stations, even outside temples. Many are sick, have little money and struggle with age-related illnesses. Often it takes weeks or months before the painful truth comes out: they were abandoned by their own families.Indian law makes it mandatory for children and relatives to care for senior citizens. Yet elder abuse and abandonment continue to rise.Why are elders being abandoned?Changing families: The joint family once had room for elders, cared for across generations. With rapid urbanisation and nuclear families, many elders are now isolated, neglected or abandoned.Poverty and poor healthcare: Small pensions and limited healthcare leave elders dependent on their families. As their health declines and costs rise, many face abuse and abandonment, especially women and widows.How our NGO partners help Our NGO partners work on the ground to rescue abandoned elders and give them shelter, care and dignity. Through old age homes across India, these seniors get to live their golden years in peace, comfort and security, surrounded by compassion.Your donation will help:Fund rescue operations to bring more elders off the streetsProvide shelter, food, healthcare, love and respectGive elders the peace of living among their peersMeet Sulochana At 70, no longer “useful” to her family, Sulochana was taken to Chennai and abandoned at a bus stand. She survived on odd jobs for six years until well-wishers brought her to our NGO partner Akshaya Trust. A medical checkup found a hearing disability, which was treated. Today, she has spent two happy years at Akshaya Trust, where she’s known for her kind heart and warm friendships with other residents.No elder should spend their final years alone. Donate today and give an abandoned senior safety, care and hope.

campaigns.title: Help Disabled Children with Shelter & Care
campaigns.description: Over 20% of the world’s blind people live in India.India has an estimated 4.95 million blind people and 70 million people with vision impairment, including around 2.4 lakh blind children. Disability and poverty often go hand in hand, and for visually impaired children the struggle is even harder. Many face cruel stigma in their own homes and are pushed into isolation.What disabled children faceStigma and misconceptions: Many disabled children are abandoned at birth or face a lifelong struggle. Blindness is often seen as a tragedy, and many believe the disabled can’t study, work or care for themselves. With the right training and tools, they can do nearly everything sighted people can.A struggle for the basics: “How will a disabled person work?” This question keeps talented people out of jobs. Even educated candidates face silent rejection, not because they can’t perform, but because employers won’t include them.How our NGO partners help Our NGO partners give blind and disabled children and young adults shelter, care and education, equipping those overlooked by their families and society with the skills to build a better life.Your donation will help:Fund the rescue of blind and disabled children abandoned by their ownProvide shelter, food, healthcare and educationEquip blind children and young adults with skills for a bright futureMeet Rani Rani, from a small village in Bihar’s Champaran district, lost her eyesight at just four. Years of discrimination followed, but she never gave up on her dream of an education. Seeing her determination, the National Association for the Blind, Delhi supported her higher studies. Today Rani is pursuing her graduation at Miranda House, Delhi, balancing academics and co-curriculars. “If you have the will, you can achieve anything,” she says.Donate today and help a blind or disabled child build the future they deserve.

campaigns.title: Feed the Hungry and Restore Hope
campaigns.description: India ranked 105th of 127 countries in the Global Hunger Index 2024.The Government of India is actively working to fight hunger, and has questioned external reports like the GHI. But for many vulnerable people, empty stomachs remain a daily reality that can’t be overlooked. Whether it’s a school-going child, a child in a slum or a destitute elder, everyone deserves a meal.What hunger feels likeFor the elderly and destitute: Already weak and in pain, many endure abandonment and hunger together. Hunger takes away their dignity and any hope of a decent life.For children in slums and schools: An empty stomach makes it hard to learn and focus, stunting growth and futures. Children suffer the quiet humiliation of falling behind their peers.How our NGO partners help Our NGO partners work on the front lines to deliver more than meals. They bring dignity in a time of need, hope in a moment of despair, and strength for a better tomorrow.Your donation will help:Provide daily nutritious meals to vulnerable communitiesKeep children in school with full stomachs and focused mindsBring dignity and care to forgotten eldersMeet Anand Anand’s parents work hard, but putting food on the table is a daily struggle. He used to sit through class distracted by hunger. Then our NGO partner Prasanna Trust, supported by donors like you, launched a daily breakfast programme. Today, Anand and thousands of children like him start their day nourished, confident and ready to learn.Hunger doesn’t discriminate, and neither should our compassion. Donate today so no child, elder or family goes to bed hungry.

campaigns.title: Help Save Young Girls From Trafficking
campaigns.description: 71.4% of missing children in India are girls.Human trafficking in India is a horrifying crisis. Over 10,659 cases were reported between 2018 and 2022, and experts believe this is only a fraction of the reality. Many missing girls end up in red-light areas. Girls as young as 12 are sold for as little as a few thousand rupees.What trafficked girls and women go throughForced into red-light areas: Lured by false promises or sold by their own families, girls endure sexual exploitation, violence and stigma in brothels, with no way out and their childhoods stolen.Trapped in modern slavery: Women and girls are beaten, starved and isolated. Debt bondage and threats keep them imprisoned in plain sight.How our NGO partners help Our NGO partners work to stop trafficking before it happens, aid rescues from red-light areas, and rebuild lives through shelter, trauma care, legal help, education and livelihood support.Your donation will help:Prevent trafficking in vulnerable communitiesFund rescue operationsRehabilitate survivors with shelter, counselling, legal aid and a path to independenceMeet Sangeeta (name changed) Sangeeta, 14, from a poor family in Varanasi, went missing after Republic Day in January 2024. Despite an FIR, police action was delayed, and she was trafficked to Telangana. Four months later, our NGO partner Guria India helped rescue her, ensured the accused was arrested and opposed his bail. Today Sangeeta is back with her family and in school. A chargesheet has been filed, and Guria continues to support the family with counselling and legal help as the trial approaches.Donate today and help a girl escape exploitation and start again with freedom and dignity.
